question:
A rectangular field has a perimeter of $80\ \text{m}$.

(a) Express its area as a function of one side.

(b) Using the second derivative test, determine the dimensions for which its area is maximum.

(c) Calculate the maximum possible area.
explanation:
(a)
Let the length and breadth of the rectangle be $x\ \text{m}$ and $y\ \text{m}$, respectively. Since the perimeter is $80\ \text{m}$,
$$2(x+y)=80$$
$$x+y=40$$
$$y=40-x$$
Therefore, the area is
$$A(x)=x(40-x)=40x-x^2$$
where $0
(b)
$$A'(x)=40-2x$$
For a stationary value,
$$40-2x=0$$
$$x=20$$
Also,
$$A''(x)=-2<0$$
Therefore, by the second derivative test, the area is maximum at $x=20$. The corresponding breadth is
$$y=40-20=20\ \text{m}$$
Thus, the rectangle must be a square of side $20\ \text{m}$.

(c)
The maximum area is
$$A(20)=20(20)=400\ \text{m}^2$$
